title: Conformant planning
description: A plan of t moves that takes a robot to the goal from every start cell, without observations; bounded conformant planning is Sigma-2-complete (Baral, Kreinovich and Trejo). Each counterexample is a start cell, and the part #program refine(k) adds a copy of the robot that starts there and must reach the goal (Shape 3). At most 15 counterexamples can occur, while the Reference run removes 65,536 plans one by one; try t = 9 (63 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The room, the moves and the horizon. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
free(X,Y) :- cell(X,Y), not pillar(X,Y).
% The four moves; t steps.
dir(e,1,0). dir(w,-1,0). dir(n,0,1). dir(s,0,-1).
step(1..t).
% to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2): moving in direction D from (X,Y) leads to (X2,Y2). A move against
% a wall or the pillar leaves the robot where it is.
to(X,Y,D,X+DX,Y+DY) :- free(X,Y), dir(D,DX,DY), free(X+DX,Y+DY).
to(X,Y,D,X,Y)       :- free(X,Y), dir(D,DX,DY), not free(X+DX,Y+DY).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any sequence of t moves.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: one move per step. Nothing else is required at first.
1 { do(T,D) : dir(D,_,_) } 1 :- step(T).
#show do/2.

fragments.name: refine
fragments.description: Grounded once per counterexample: the plan must also work from that start cell.
fragments.text:
#program refine(k).
% cex(k,start(X,Y)): the k-th counterexample is a start cell. Follow the plan from there ...
at(k,X,Y,0) :- cex(k,start(X,Y)).
at(k,X2,Y2,T) :- at(k,X,Y,T-1), do(T,D), to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2).
% ... it has to end in the goal.
:- goal(X,Y), not at(k,X,Y,t).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the moves of the plan.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a start cell from which the plan does not reach the goal (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a start cell from which the plan ends somewhere else.
1 { start(X,Y) : free(X,Y) } 1.
at(X,Y,0) :- start(X,Y).
at(X2,Y2,T) :- at(X,Y,T-1), do(T,D), to(X,Y,D,X2,Y2).
:- goal(X,Y), at(X,Y,t).
#show start/2.
% No relevant/1 rules: the loop passes the start cell to the refine part.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction + refine
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(start/2))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

instances.facts:
% A robot in a 4 x 4 room with one pillar. It does not know where it starts.
cell(1..4,1..4).
pillar(2,3).
goal(2,2).

% The example room with t = 7: too short, no plan.
cell(1..4,1..4).
pillar(2,3).
goal(2,2).

% A 3 x 3 room without a pillar; the goal is a corner.
cell(1..3,1..3).
#defined pillar/2.
goal(1,1).

% A corridor of 5 x 1 cells; the goal is in the middle. Moves n and s do nothing.
cell(1..5,1).
#defined pillar/2.
goal(3,1).
